_comment: Pins are authored deliberately and never generated from a run.
A MEASUREMENT pin sits at the current number: it cannot fail on anything
that exists today, only on new dead content. That is the ratchet stopping
regrowth, and it does not by itself force work.
A TARGET pin is set where the number should be. The section is EXPECTED to
sit out of band until the work lands; that is the point of it.
A pin may carry both a limit and a target: the limit fails the build, the
target states the direction of travel. There is no third kind — the
presence of both max and target is the signal, and the shape says so.
`kind` is a note for whoever reads this file. The generator branches on the
section's DIRECTION, declared in status.py, and never on `kind`. A pin key
naming no section is refused rather than silently doing nothing.
A pin with a `source` block does not hold its own numbers. The edge lives
as a constexpr in the test that asserts it, and this file names the symbol;
status.py reads it there. Seven edges used to exist in both places and
could disagree in silence — and the at-cap entry below anticipates its own
band moving, which would have left the test asserting the old edges while
this report went green. Same direction as the lane register, and the same
reason: the script is a reporter and a reporter must not be an authority.
A `source` naming a symbol that does not exist is REFUSED at exit 2, which
is the discipline this file already applies to a pin key naming no section
— refuse rather than silently do nothing. The `why` prose stays here: the
number is an assertion and belongs beside the code, the DECISION to move it
is what this file records.
RE-PINNING IS NOT WIDENING, AND THE DIFFERENCE IS WHETHER SOMEONE LOOKED.
Raising a ceiling because a section went red is widening: it converts a
failure into a pass and answers a question by not asking it. Moving a pin
after a reviewed, deliberate change is maintenance: the number moved for a
reason a person read and accepted. The test is not the size of the move, it
is whether the reason was examined before the pin followed it.
_expected_red_comment: Deliberate reds, enumerated. A red test not on this list is a regression.
ADD THE ENTRY IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT ADDS THE TEST. Otherwise the build
goes red as an unexpected regression, and the fastest-looking fix is to
revert the test — which deletes the finding it was written to hold.
Each entry names the finding it encodes and the condition that deletes it.
AN ENTRY CAN ALSO BE DELETED BECAUSE THE MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG, and three
were: trash TTK, elite TTK and the boss band all measured a rifle dealing
13 damage where the shipped rifle deals 24, and the boss test composed a
boss rank onto a trash archetype the game never fields. Correcting the two
reads moved nothing in the game and turned all three green. That is the
reason the remaining five each say what they READ as well as what they
assert: a deliberate red is a claim about the game, and it is only worth
the name if the instrument behind it was checked first.
One promoted finding is still owed a test: archetype spread — and it is
now known to be unwritable as specified, because four of the five classes
author no stat effects at all, so the invariant it would encode is false
by construction rather than merely unmet.
_expected_red: Progression.PowerBand.AbilityLane :: Ability parity measures 0.641x at the cap against O99's ruled 0.85-1.15x, and 0.38x at endgame where the section is unpinned. An ability-geared build's ability lane composes to 64% of a weapon-geared build's weapon lane at the same gear depth, and the deficit WIDENS with gear depth rather than diluting - a lane with more lines compounds harder up a back-loaded ladder. Crit and More cancel exactly; the shortfall is flat 1.000 against 1.154 and increased 3.35 against 4.49. DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: ability affix breadth is authored, the flat-half question is answered, and the cap measurement reaches the band. Do not close it by widening the band, and do not close it by letting ability hits read the weapon pool - that is the partition deleted, not the gap closed. MOVED AND CAME BACK, 2026-08-23/24. O95 replaced Culling's never-selected x1.18 More with an UNCONDITIONAL +18% WeaponDamage line, which took at-cap 6.53 -> 6.79 and parity 0.647 -> 0.622 on that one edit. A doctrine node moving two Core-level metrics is a doctrine doing Core's job, and the ruling that followed says so: a doctrine may not author a magnitude on a generic damage pool unless it is conditional on that doctrine's own axis. Culling's line is now gated on Aiming, which is Marksman's axis and is NOT one of the three conditions the fixture measures in (Airborne, RecentlyDashed, Redline) -- so it leaves the measurement entirely and both figures returned EXACTLY: 6.53 and 0.647. Three further unconditional generic-damage lines were then conditioned for the same reason (AmmunitionEconomy to Redline, LongLens and PierceDiscipline to Aiming), which is the whole of the remaining drift: at-cap 6.53 -> 6.54 and parity 0.647 -> 0.641. Redline IS in the measurement state, so AmmunitionEconomy's 5% stayed live and moved at-cap up a hundredth; the two Aiming lines left the measurement and cost parity six thousandths. Neither is content getting weaker -- the lines pay exactly as much, to a player who aims.

Progression.PowerBand.AtCap :: The at-cap band measures 6.54x against an authored 8-10x, on a baseline definition corrected 2026-08-22 (a realistically decent roll two tiers below what item level allows, derived identically at both measurement points; it was previously the theoretical worst roll, which made the number uninterpretable). DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: content retunes upward until the measurement reaches the authored 8-10x. RULED (ORDERS ruling 5, 2026-08-25): 'we will tune power up' -- the band does not move, the assertion does not widen, and the pin stays open pointed at content. MOVED AND CAME BACK, 2026-08-23/24. O95 replaced Culling's never-selected x1.18 More with an UNCONDITIONAL +18% WeaponDamage line, which took at-cap 6.53 -> 6.79 and parity 0.647 -> 0.622 on that one edit. A doctrine node moving two Core-level metrics is a doctrine doing Core's job, and the ruling that followed says so: a doctrine may not author a magnitude on a generic damage pool unless it is conditional on that doctrine's own axis. Culling's line is now gated on Aiming, which is Marksman's axis and is NOT one of the three conditions the fixture measures in (Airborne, RecentlyDashed, Redline) -- so it leaves the measurement entirely and both figures returned EXACTLY: 6.53 and 0.647. Three further unconditional generic-damage lines were then conditioned for the same reason (AmmunitionEconomy to Redline, LongLens and PierceDiscipline to Aiming), which is the whole of the remaining drift: at-cap 6.53 -> 6.54 and parity 0.647 -> 0.641. Redline IS in the measurement state, so AmmunitionEconomy's 5% stayed live and moved at-cap up a hundredth; the two Aiming lines left the measurement and cost parity six thousandths. Neither is content getting weaker -- the lines pay exactly as much, to a player who aims.

Items.Drops.DropChanceReachesEveryRank :: The Drop Chance affix does NOTHING on a boss, and nearly nothing on a modifier-bearing elite. GetEffectiveDropChance is Clamp(Base * (1 + Bonus), 0, 1) and BossDropChance is authored at 1.0, already the top of its own ClampMax -- so a boss drops on every kill with no affix at all and every point of Drop Chance a player ever rolled buys exactly zero there. ModifierBearing at 0.90 saturates on an 11% roll. BreakerDropTable.h names this failure at the affix's own declaration: a stat printed as Drop Chance that changed nothing you were getting anyway is 'the kind of quiet lie this project has shipped before'. SECOND CONSEQUENCE, and the reason it matters beyond the affix: a probability cannot exceed 1.0, so against a 0.10 trash floor the drop-chance AXIS cannot express a difficulty ratio above 10x at any tuning. It is a saturated scale rather than a tuned value, which is precisely why the Boss row disagrees with its own Riftglass row by 11x -- and any reward composition built on it inherits that ceiling. DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: the affix layer answers it. THE FIX IS NOT IN THIS LAYER AND MUST NOT BE ATTEMPTED FROM IT -- the affix system has one owner at a time and is being worked independently, so nothing here may touch Items/BreakerAffixLibrary or add a defensive-chance affix to route around this. What this entry is FOR is that the finding survives the handover: the assertion is layer-neutral (a visible stat must do something at every rank) and it will go green from the affix side without anything being edited here. The shape offered and not built: where a rank's base chance saturates, the clamped-away surplus converts to quantity and then to a rarity floor, one step per full multiple of unusable headroom -- the same move O75 makes for an elite at three modifiers, at the other end of the range. Recorded as an option, owned elsewhere.

Abilities.Catalogue.Partition :: Swift registers seven abilities (O175) while the class-definition buckets in Progression/BreakerProgressionLibrary.cpp still partition four. DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: LEDGER lands O176's two lines -- :4180 starters {Swift.Slipcut, Swift.Skim}, :4186 unlockables {Swift.Lead, Swift.CadenceBreak, Swift.HardStop, Swift.Sightline} -- alongside KIT's DefaultAbilityIdForSlot flip. Do not close it by unregistering the abilities.

Abilities.Catalogue.NoPermanentlyRefusable :: Swift.Slipcut, Swift.HardStop and Swift.Sightline are registered, offered by the derived picker, and refused by every unlock path until O176's unlockable rows exist -- exactly the stranded state O100 named, here deliberately for one landing window. DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: the same LEDGER edit as Abilities.Catalogue.Partition lands.

Progression.AbilityUnlocks.ReachableByFifty :: The three O175 Swift abilities cannot be bought until they are in UnlockableAbilityIds; the token schedule needs no edit (the clamp untruncates itself at four). DELETE THIS ENTRY WHEN: the same LEDGER edit as Abilities.Catalogue.Partition lands.

silent-nodes.why: RE-PINNED 47 -> 54 AS A CORRECTION, NOT A WIDENING. The consumer index was a raw text scan of production source INCLUDING COMMENTS, so a tag named in a WAITING-ON roster counted as a consumer and its node reported live. Six independent per-tree audits read the CONSUMERS rather than the report: Core.Slice 3 -> 5 silent, Swift Kinetic/Marksman/Frenzy 1/2/2 -> 3/1/1, Gunsmith Armory/FieldTech/Tinkerer 2/1/2 -> 3/0/1. The scan now strips comments and keeps string literals, and it also resolves a tag through the full "Progression.Node..." string an accessor requests, which moved two tags the other way. 47 was never a real 47. Drive this down regardless: a node a player spends a point on and gets nothing from is a broken promise, and it is the failure this project has shipped four times.

dead-tags.why: RE-PINNED 118 -> 143 AS A CORRECTION. Same cause as silent-nodes: the index read comments, so every tag listed in a WAITING-ON roster counted as consumed. It also ran the other way -- Node_Overpenetration and Node_MarksmanCalledShot ARE consumed, at BreakerWeaponComponent.cpp:1811 and :1417, through accessors that request the tag by its full string and never name the identifier. Both directions are now matched. 143 of 202 is not all rot: some is deliberate reserve ahead of consumers, which O72 makes the required order. Nobody has separated reserve from backlog, and until someone does this pin only stops the number growing.

unmapped-stat-targets.why: Lowered 7 -> 6 by wiring DashCooldown, which was never blocked on anything: the comment recording it as unwireable claimed EBreakerAggregatedAttribute had no dash entry, and it had one when that was written. Before that, lowered 8 -> 7 when the section stopped counting rider-delivered targets as unmapped: O98 rules MeleeDamage a tag-keyed slice of the weapon pool, so it will never have a lane and counting it made a ratcheting ceiling that could not reach zero. Before that, lowered 10 -> 8 by the O54 pool split, which wired WeaponDamage and AbilityDamage. They were the only entries ever blocked on something larger than a line of aggregation: there was ONE damage bucket and a partition needs two. A ceiling that does not fall after a real drop has stopped being a ratchet.

empty-lanes.why:
Raised 8 -> 9 by wiring DashCooldown. Worth stating because it was predicted NOT to move, on the reasoning that gear already bids into DashCooldownReduction: this section counts NODE authors, not bidders, so a lane gear bids into still reads empty until a node reaches it. That is the section working -- the tree is the layer it measures. Before that, raised 6 -> 8, and this is the one shape of increase the pin file permits: O72 orders the work as vocabulary first, then authoring, so a newly wired lane necessarily lands here for exactly as long as it takes content to reach it. 

THE WORKED EXAMPLE FOR O72, MEASURED 2026-08-24, and the strongest evidence that rule has. Nine Caster tier-4 nodes were authored as rules-as-tags, which is the honest posture for Mana-loop rewrites the stat enum cannot express. Merged FIRST, they moved three ceilings by exactly nine each -- silent-nodes 52 -> 61, dead-tags 143 -> 152, scaffolding-nodes 50 -> 59 -- and would have needed a ruling to widen all three. Then the order was reversed: SB10's READER landed first, with its tag declared ahead of the node that will grant it. Declared tags went 202 -> 203 and dead-tags HELD at 143, because the tag arrived already consumed; silent-nodes and scaffolding did not move at all, because no node had arrived. 

Same nine nodes, same content, opposite outcome, decided entirely by which half lands first. A tag declared with a reader and no node is honest -- the rule works, nothing grants it yet. A node granting a tag nothing reads is the failure this project has shipped four times. That is O72 as arithmetic rather than as advice, and it is why 'author the readers first' is an ordering rule and not a preference.

uncalled-generation.why: THE ZERO THIS PIN RECORDED WAS NOT REAL. The check counted a hook's own DEFINITION as one of its callers -- hooks are harvested from Classes/*.h so the self-exclusion compared against the header, while the .cpp holding the body stayed in the search set and matched itself. Every one of the eighteen listed its own component .cpp as a caller, so the section reported zero and could not have reported anything else. The pin note used to read 'the number did not move, which is the answer worth recording'; it had not moved because it could not. Corrected, the true figure is THREE: BreakerChargeComponent::NotifyAssist, which has no caller anywhere including tests, and BreakerScrapComponent's NotifyAmmoPickupOverflow and NotifyAmmoReturnedOnKill, which are called only from the suite. THE CEILING STAYS AT ZERO on purpose -- it is the target, the section is legitimately out of band, and it closes by wiring three hooks to the events that should fire them, never by re-pinning to three.

unimplemented-invariants.why: Re-pinned 43 -> 42: UI.NoItemScore got its test, and it was VIOLATED at the time -- the loadout subtitle printed the sum of equipped item levels as a gear score, on the most-used screen in the game, under an invariant asserting no screen prints one. Third worked example in a week for this target. THE WORKED EXAMPLE THIS TARGET EXISTS FOR is UI.Damage.Aggregation and UI.Damage.Cap. Two named invariants, no tests, and the feature they describe was ALREADY BUILT -- so it looked done, and three of the rule's four clauses were wrong in the shipped tuning for as long as nobody measured them: a damage-over-time effect that could never merge with itself, two deliberate shots that merged into one, a window that slid so a held trigger accumulated a whole magazine, and a cap that evicted the busiest number first. An untested invariant is not a gap in coverage, it is a claim nobody has checked, and the more finished the feature looks the longer it survives. That is the argument for 43 -> 20. Re-pinned 45 -> 43: UI.Damage.Aggregation and UI.Damage.Cap got their tests. Both described behaviour that already EXISTED and was wrong in three of its four clauses, which is the state an untested invariant is worst in -- it looks asserted, the feature looks built, and nothing is watching the tuning. Before that, re-pinned 46 -> 45: Progression.WorldPoints.SoloReachable got its test, and it could not have had one before -- O7 rules fifteen world Core Points canon and they had no representation in code at all, so there was nothing to assert over. A ceiling that does not fall after a real drop has stopped being a ratchet. Before that, re-pinned 48 -> 46 as two of the three promoted findings got their tests — HitsToDie and BossBand, both red on purpose and both enumerated above. ArchetypeSpread is the third and is still owed. Before that, re-pinned 51 -> 48: PowerBand.AbilityLane was written by the O54 pool split, and the split added two invariants to power-and-scaling that landed WITH their tests rather than ahead of them. Pinned so it cannot grow, targeted so it does not sit there for a year. Order: the four promoted findings first; then anything guarding a newly written and therefore unenforced rule — the three-pool model, the rewrite caps, the axis-overlap prohibition, equip caps at save load; then the rest, with the systems they describe.

loot-per-hour.why: The reference figure the drop pipeline is tuned against, at the reference area level. Band rather than ceiling: too few items is as wrong as too many.

power-band-atcap.why: Whether 8-10x was ever derived or seeded is an open question; the pin holds the authored target until it is answered. THE MEASUREMENT IS NOT RESTATED HERE, on purpose: this why-text used to open "Measures 6.53x on the corrected baseline", and that was a third hand-typed copy of a number the suite emits every run. It went stale beside a transcription in BossOptimized that had gone stale the same way, and a pin whose prose disagrees with the value beside it in the same table teaches a reader to trust the prose. The live figure is in Docs/STATE.md, computed by BreakerPowerBandTest::AtCapBand and emitted as power-band-atcap.

power-band-ability.why: O99. Measures 0.647x at the cap. THE BAND CLOSES BY AUTHORING CONTENT, NOT BY TOUCHING THE COMPOSITION. The two builds hold an identical More product and identical crit lines, so both cancel exactly and parity is the flat ratio times the increased ratio - and both are short, in two different ways. INCREASED, 3.35 against 4.49: the ability pool is one seeded line per slot at placeholder values where the weapon pool is that line plus added damage, fire rate, five conditional lines and the projectile family. That half is unauthored content. FLAT, 1.000 against 1.154: the ability lane has no flat line at all, because Added Damage bids Flat into the weapon lane only and O54 names three INCREASED pools without settling the flat half. That half is an unanswered design question and is in the open list. Anyone reading this as a plumbing problem will 'fix' it by folding the weapon pool back into ability hits, which deletes the partition rather than closing the gap. Target, not measurement: 0.647x pinned would enshrine abilities as a second-class lane, the same mistake as pinning the defence inversion at 3.76.

power-band-endgame.why: Measures 15.40x, comfortably inside. Now meaningful, because both bands finally compute their baseline the same way. DESCRIBED PER O136 as where MOST builds land, not where every build must land: the measurement here carries no rewrite by construction, and a Prolific build composing past the upper edge (22.64x) is intended feel rather than a breach -- the edge is a target, never a ceiling.

damage-vs-defence-growth.why: LANDED at 0.63 by the O116 retune: monster damage now grows x2.32 across the levelling range against gear health's x3.67, so hits-to-die rises rather than falls. Was 3.76, and pinned as a TARGET because pinning at 3.76 would have enshrined the inversion. It is a measurement ratchet now: the ceiling stays at 1.0, which is the property O91 rules rather than the number measured, so a future retune that pushes damage growth back past what defence buys fails here.

world-points-unwired.why: 14 of the 15 canon world Core Points have no trigger in the build. Only the Forge interaction does, because Kess ships with dialogue and a registered flag. This is the campaign's payout gap as a number: eight of the twenty-eight authored missions pay one of these as their entire reward, so a third of the mission list has nothing to give. Pinned at the current value so it cannot grow and targeted at zero so it does not sit here for a year. Two of the fourteen are the grouped archetype first-clears (O117), and they are narrower than they look: the eight archetypes are AUTHORED -- Clear, Sever, Hold, Hunt, Escort, Carry, Collapse, Silence, sited across missions A1-4 to A2-7 -- so the vocabulary exists and simply has no C++ representation yet. What is actually missing is ONE rift completion event to fire on. That is a different and much smaller job than authoring a vocabulary, and worth stating precisely, because 'no vocabulary exists' reads as a design gap when it is a plumbing gap.

rewrite-impact.why: Worst single rewrite step on an optimized build. RE-PINNED BY RULING (O136): the derived layer ceiling (EndgameBandMaximum / EndgameBandMid) read the band's upper edge as a ceiling, and the owner ruled it is a target -- a rewrite stacking past the edge is the intended feel, so the composed 22.64x is accepted and the only bound left on the rollable layer is its AUTHORED per-step ceiling, which for the one per-item-stacking rule is Prolific's own 1.5. This was called tautological when the section first pointed here; it is not any more, because it is now the owner's number rather than a stand-in for a band fit nobody had ruled: a future rewrite authored past 1.5 fails, and Prolific at 1.4634 is the intended margin, not 97% of an accident. The layer ceiling survives only for O96's major/minor-stack partition (RuleBandImpact.Major), which ruling 6 did not touch.

offered-to-spendable.why:
THE FLOOR CLEARS BY IDENTITY FOR EVERY DOCTRINE BUILT TO THE STANDARD SHAPE, AND THAT MAKES IT A FALSE GREEN. Twelve nodes, every one costing two points to its last rank: 12 x 2 = 24 offered against an 8-point wallet, and 24 / 8 is exactly 3.00. Not approximately -- identically, for every conforming tree, forever, whatever any individual node does. The ratio cannot vary for those trees without departing from the shape, which means it has stopped measuring authoring and started reporting the shape spec back at the reader. Swift's three trees prove it CAN vary (26-28 offered, 3.25-3.50x) and they vary only by having more nodes than the shape. 

That is the same failure as the resource-hook count: a section whose value is fixed by construction cannot report a problem. It is recorded rather than repaired here because repairing it means deciding what refusal should be MEASURED by for a doctrine, which is a design question. 

AND IT IS A CLIFF, NOT A TREND. A tree at exactly 3.00 goes red on the change that prices one node at 1 or drops a node, with no warning on any earlier run -- a pin that reads ok until the run it fails on is reporting one bit. offered-to-spendable-margin is the second bit and currently reads 9 of 16. 

WHETHER 3.0 WAS DERIVED OR SEEDED IS OPEN, and is carried in DECISIONS beside the same question against the at-cap band's 8-10x. VISION says a tree offers far more than any budget can buy; 3.00x means a character buys a third of one, and whether that is 'far more' has never been answered. Nine trees sit on the answer today and twelve will once the Caster trios merge. 

The old text here read '0.63x on the worst tree', which was two revisions stale -- the third pin why found restating a measurement it could not keep up with.

scaffolding-nodes.why: NEW SECTION, split out of node-shape-composition's note. O112 unpinned that BAND for a real reason -- 60% ranked minors means 60% unconditional stat lines and O76 gives those to affixes -- but unpinning the band took this count down with it, and a number that judges nothing is a number nobody defends. The band is genuinely unresolved; this is not. A node with no stat line, no condition and no rule anything reads is an authoring failure at any composition target, and it is the count Phase 4 writes a test against. Pinned at the first honest reading, after the comment-stripping fix.

unevaluable-conditions.why: The whole Recently* family: RecentlyKilled, RecentlyTookDamage, RecentlyCastAbility, RecentlyAppliedStatus. Each needs a recorder that binds the combat and ability events and stores a world time, the way UBreakerCharacterMovementComponent::GetLastDashTime already does for RecentlyDashed -- the working template, and the only one of the five that is live. Pinned at the current four so it can only fall; the TARGET is zero, reached by four recorders or by four enumerators deleted. This is not closable by widening the pin. Note also that the number falling is not the point: the assertion that no authored effect is gated on one of these is the half that catches the defect, and it exists because a node was nearly authored against RecentlyKilled by accident during the O95 pass. A NOTE ON THE PIN SCHEMA, recorded here because this key is where it fired: this pin was first written with 'ceiling' and 'target' keys instead of 'max' and 'kind', and status.py refused the whole report at exit 2 with 'is a ceiling and is missing max. The unset edge would never be checked.' That is the guard working exactly as intended -- a malformed pin that silently checked nothing would be a section reporting ok because it had no edge to fail against, which is the same defect as a check that cannot move.
